families.summary: Fully automated post-processing software that classifies views, segments and annotates transthoracic echo DICOM images (2D, M-mode, PW/CW/tissue Doppler) and produces an editable measurement report. Us2.v1 (K210791, 2021) was validated against Brigham and Women's core-lab triplicate reads in 600 studies using an individual equivalence coefficient non-inferiority margin of 0.25; Us2.v2 (K233676, 2024) added LV global and regional longitudinal strain, RV tissue Doppler, TAPSE, aortic root and LVOT/aortic valve Doppler parameters, validated by RMSE (strain vs GE EchoPAC) and ICC in three US datasets (n=3029, 260, 192) spanning 8 ultrasound vendors.
families.intended_use_quote: Us2.v2 is an image post-processing analysis software device used for viewing and quantifying cardiovascular ultrasound images in DI COM format. The device is intended to aid diagnostic review and analysis of echocardiographic data, patient record management and reporting.
families.indications_for_use_quote: Us2.v2 software is used to process acquired transthoracic cardiac ultrasound images, to analyze and make measurements on images in order to provide automated estimation of several cardiac structural and functional parameters, including left/ right atrial and ventricular linear dimensions, volumes, systolic function and diastolic function, measured by B mode, M mode and Doppler (PW, CW, tissue) modalities. The data produced by this software is intended to be used to support qualified cardiologists, sonographers, or other licensed professional healthcare practitioners for clinical decision-making. Us2.v2 is indicated for use in adult patients.
embedded_ai_features: Automated 2D, M-mode and Doppler measurements (LV/RV/LA/RA dimensions, volumes, LVEF biplane MOD, E/A, e', E/e', TR Vmax; v2 adds LV GLS (A4C/A3C/A2C) and regional strain, TAPSE, RV E'/A'/S', LVOT diameter and PW Doppler, CW aortic valve Doppler, AVA, VR, sinotubular junction, sinus of Valsalva)
Guideline reference-range comparison and automated report generation

clearances.changes_summary: Initial clearance of Us2.v1 (model V1.0.0). Predicate: EchoMD Automated Ejection Fraction Software (Bay Labs/Caption Health, K173780, product code LLZ). Subject device provides many more automated measurements than the predicate's ejection fraction (LV Doppler/tissue Doppler, biplane volumes/LVEF, linear dimensions, RV/LA/RA dimensions, TR Vmax); manual editing performed in the application rather than on a PACS workstation.
notable_flags: Reviewed by Division of Radiological Health (OHT7)
Retrospective validation vs Brigham and Women's core lab
Indicated for adults; not validated for congenital, valve, pericardial disease or intra-cardiac lesions

clearances.changes_summary: Us2.v2 (model V2.0.0) uses Us2.v1 as predicate. Automated calculations are 'Same as the predicate plus': LV GLS, A4C/A3C/A2C LV GLS, LV regional strain, TAPSE, RV E'/A'/S', aortic sinotubular junction and sinus of Valsalva, LVOT diameter, PW LVOT Vmax/VTI/Pmax/Pmean, CW AoV Vmax/VTI/Pmax/Pmean, AVA and VR (p.7 table). Indications broadened to list B-mode, M-mode and Doppler modalities and to support 'sonographers, or other licensed professional healthcare practitioners' in addition to cardiologists; the v1 statement that the device 'has not been validated for ... valve disease' is no longer in the IFU. Validation switched from IEC to RMSE (strain vs GE EchoPAC) and ICC.
notable_flags: Reviewed by DHT 8B, OHT 8: Office of Radiological Health (letter p.2)
Tested on data from 8 ultrasound vendors

performance_claims.endpoint: Interchangeability of 23 automated parameters with core-lab readers (published pivotal study)
performance_claims.value: All IEC point estimates <0; upper bound of 95% CI <0.25
performance_claims.comparator: Three repeated measurements by core lab sonographers
performance_claims.dataset_description: Tromp J et al., Nat Commun 2022 (doi 10.1038/s41467-022-34245-1); same 600-subject cohort (421 HF / 179 controls) as the K210791 validation study. Note the paper reports 69% women whereas the FDA summary Table 1 reports 72.6%/67.4% male; discrepancy unresolved.
performance_claims.quote: Among 602 anonymised echocardiographic studies from 600 people (421 with heart failure, 179 controls, 69% women), the point estimates of IEC are all <0 and the upper bound of the 95% confidence intervals below 0.25, indicating that the disagreement between the deep learning and human measures is lower than the disagreement among three core lab readers.

performance_claims.endpoint: LVEF and LV volume agreement in external datasets (algorithm-development paper)
performance_claims.value: MAE 9-25 mL for LV volumes, 6-10% for LVEF, 1.8-2.2 for E/e'; AUC 0.90-0.92 for LVEF<40%, 0.91 for E/e'>=13
performance_claims.comparator: Locally measured manual values (Alberta HEART, Taiwan real-world, EchoNet-Dynamic)
performance_claims.dataset_description: Tromp J et al., Lancet Digit Health 2022 (doi 10.1016/S2589-7500(21)00235-1): training 1145 echos + internal test 406 (ATTRaCT); external Alberta HEART n=1029, Taiwan n=31,241, EchoNet-Dynamic n=10,030, prospective n=142.
performance_claims.quote: In the external datasets (n=1029 to 10 030 echocardiograms used as input), automated measurements showed good agreement with locally measured values, with a mean absolute error range of 9-25 mL for left ventricular volumes, 6-10% for left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), and 1·8-2·2 for the ratio of the mitral inflow E wave to the tissue Doppler e' wave (E/e' ratio); and reliably classified systolic dysfunction (LVEF <40%, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC] range 0·90-0·92) and diastolic dysfunction (E/e' ratio ≥13, AUC range 0·91-0·91), with narrow 95% CIs for AUC values.

performance_claims.endpoint: Automated GLS vs manual GLS, external validation (strain paper)
performance_claims.comparator: Manual GLS measurements (real-world Taiwan cohort; PROMIS-HFpEF core lab)
performance_claims.dataset_description: Myhre PL et al., Eur Heart J Digit Health 2024 (doi 10.1093/ehjdh/ztad072): DL workflow analysed 3741 (89%) Taiwanese studies, 176 (96%) PROMIS-HFpEF, 158 (98%) HMC-QU-MI; regional strain AUC 0.80 for wall-motion abnormalities.
performance_claims.quote: Automated GLS showed good agreement with manual measurements (mean ± SD): -18.9 ± 4.5% vs. -18.2 ± 4.4%, respectively, bias 0.68 ± 2.52%, MAD 2.0 ± 1.67, RMSE = 2.61, R = 0.84 in the Taiwanese cohort; and -15.4 ± 4.1% vs. -15.9 ± 3.6%, respectively, bias -0.65 ± 2.71%, MAD 2.19 ± 1.71, RMSE = 2.78, R = 0.76 in PROMIS-HFpEF.

performance_claims.endpoint: Detection of LVEF <=40% from AI-analysed handheld echo vs expert cart-based echo
performance_claims.value: Accuracy 0.93 (95% CI 0.90-0.95); IEC -0.40 (95% CI -0.60, -0.16) for cart-based LVEF interchangeability
performance_claims.comparator: Human expert analysis of cart-based TTE
performance_claims.dataset_description: Campbell RT et al., Eur J Heart Fail 2025 (doi 10.1002/ejhf.3783); multicentre prospective observational study, suspected HF; AI produced an LVEF in 61% of handheld and 77% of cart-based scans. Full text (PMC12803686) states handheld and cart scans were reported by Us2.ai software version 1.4.1 (Philips Lumify handheld; GE Vivid E95 cart).
performance_claims.quote: The AI-automated analysis of handheld echocardiography had a diagnostic accuracy of 0.93 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.90, 0.95) for identifying LVEF ≤40% (compared to the human analysis of cart-based transthoracic echocardiography scans). AI-automated analysis of LVEF on handheld devices was interchangeable with cart-based LVEF reported by two expert humans (IEC -0.40, 95% CI -0.60, -0.16).

performance_claims.endpoint: Detection of LVEF <50% by AI-enhanced novice handheld pathway
performance_claims.value: AUC 0.880 (95% CI 0.802-0.958); sensitivity 84.6%, specificity 91.4%, PPV 78.5%, NPV 94.1%; median absolute LVEF deviation 6.03%
performance_claims.comparator: Standard echo by trained sonographers interpreted by cardiologists
performance_claims.dataset_description: Huang W et al., Sci Rep 2024 (doi 10.1038/s41598-024-62467-4), PANES-HF: EchoNous Kosmos handheld acquisition by novices with Us2.ai automated reporting; n=100 symptomatic suspected-HF patients, 27 with LVEF<50%.
performance_claims.quote: The area under the curve (AUC) of the AI novice pathway was 0.880 (95% CI 0.802, 0.958). The sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive and negative predictive values of the AI-enhanced novice pathway in detecting LVEF < 50% were 84.6%, 91.4%, 78.5% and 94.1% respectively. The median absolute deviation of the AI-novice pathway LVEF from the reference standard LVEF was 6.03%.

performance_claims.endpoint: Aortic stenosis Doppler parameters vs blinded human readers
performance_claims.value: AV peak velocity r=0.97; mean gradient r=0.94; AVA (continuity) r=0.88; SVi r=0.79; LVOT VTI r=0.89; AV VTI r=0.96; LVOT diameter r=0.76 (all P<.001)
performance_claims.comparator: Manual measurements by trained echocardiographers blinded to AI
performance_claims.dataset_description: Krishna H et al., J Am Soc Echocardiogr 2023 (doi 10.1016/j.echo.2023.03.008); 256 patients, normal valves through all AS severities; single-center.
performance_claims.quote: Across all AS severities, AI closely matched human measurement of aortic valve peak velocity (r = 0.97, P < .001), mean pressure gradient (r = 0.94, P < .001), aortic valve area by continuity equation (r = 0.88, P < .001), stroke volume index (r = 0.79, P < .001), left ventricular outflow tract velocity-time integral (r = 0.89, P < .001), aortic valve velocity-time integral (r = 0.96, P < .001), and left ventricular outflow tract diameter (r = 0.76, P < .001).

performance_claims.endpoint: Sonographer workflow with AI-automated analysis (randomized crossover trial)
performance_claims.value: 13.0+/-3.5 vs 14.3+/-4.2 min per exam (P<0.001); 16.7+/-2.5 vs 14.1+/-2.5 exams/day (P=0.003); AI values agreed with expert-endorsed values within clinical limits for 90% of parameters
performance_claims.comparator: Manual sonographer workflow (non-AI days)
performance_claims.dataset_description: Sakamoto A et al., J Am Heart Assoc 2026 (doi 10.1161/JAHA.125.045637), AI-Echo RCT, single-center Japan, 4 sonographers, 585 patients over 38 days (AI days 317; non-AI days 268). The abstract does not name the vendor; the full text (PMC12909003) states the AI tool was the US2.ai platform (Us2.ai, Singapore) and that M3AI, its Japanese distributor, provided software and two co-authors.
performance_claims.quote: AI assistance significantly reduced examination time (13.0±3.5 minutes versus 14.3±4.2 minutes, P<0.001) and increased the number of daily examinations (16.7±2.5 versus 14.1±2.5, P=0.003). The number of echocardiographic parameters per examination increased 3.4-fold on AI days (85±12 versus 25±1, P<0.001).

performance_claims.endpoint: LVOT, sinotubular junction and sinus of Valsalva diameters vs cardiac MRI (independent validation)

performance_claims.quote: Artificial intelligence-derived measurements demonstrated comparable agreement with CMR: ICC 0.70 (95% CI: 0.61-0.77) for LVOT, 0.77 (95% 0.70-0.83) for STJ, and 0.77 (95% 0.70-0.83) for SoV.

performance_claims.subgroup_notes: Accuracy reported as maintained across LVEF and LAVi subcategories.
performance_claims.quote: For LVGLS, the ICC was 0.83 (95% CI: 0.77-0.88) and 0.77 (95% CI: 0.67-0.84) for LASr.

performance_claims.endpoint: TR jet velocity vs manual measurement and PH detection (independent validation)
performance_claims.value: TRJV measured in 87% of echocardiograms; ICC 0.94 (95% CI 0.94-0.95); AUC for PH 0.88 (95% CI 0.84-0.90) automated vs 0.88 (0.86-0.91) manual
performance_claims.comparator: Manual TRJV; right heart catheterisation (mPAP >20 mmHg) as PH reference
performance_claims.dataset_description: Salehi M et al., ERJ Open Res 2025 (doi 10.1183/23120541.00592-2024): ASPIRE registry, 1031 consecutive patients investigated for suspected PH 2009-2021 with echo and RHC; 771 (75%) had PH.
performance_claims.quote: The AI tool demonstrated high interpretation yield, successfully measuring TRJV in 87% of echocardiograms. Manually and automatically derived TRJV values showed excellent agreement (intraclass correlation coefficient 0.94, 95% CI 0.94-0.95) with minimal bias (Bland-Altman analysis). Automated TRJV measurements showed equally high diagnostic accuracy for PH as manual measurements (area under the curve 0.88, 95% CI 0.84-0.90 versus 0.88, 95% CI 0.86-0.91).

performance_claims.endpoint: Peri-operative anaesthetist-acquired echo analysed by US2.AI vs clinician measurements (multicentre)
performance_claims.value: ICC 0.605-0.956 across 10 parameters; LVEF r=0.845, mean difference -1.9%; LV systolic function classified correctly in 180/201 (91%), diastolic dysfunction in 193/201 (96%)
performance_claims.comparator: Manual measurements by echocardiography-certified anaesthetists
performance_claims.dataset_description: Borde DP et al., Anaesthesia 2026 (doi 10.1111/anae.70235): prospective multicentre observational study; 12-view protocol; 202/206 (98%) analysable.
performance_claims.subgroup_notes: All 10 pulmonary hypertension and 6 severe aortic stenosis cases identified; IVC collapsibility (r=0.641) and cardiac output (r=0.675) agreement moderate.
performance_claims.quote: Agreement between artificial intelligence- and clinician-derived continuous measurements was good to excellent for most parameters, with intraclass correlation coefficient values 0.605-0.956 (p < 0.001). Left ventricular ejection fraction was strongly correlated (r = 0.845, p < 0.001) with a mean difference of -1.9%. The US2.AI software classified left ventricular systolic function correctly in 180/201 (91%) patients and left ventricular diastolic dysfunction in 193/201 (96%) patients.

training_data.description: Neither FDA summary states a training set size; both state only that test data were strictly segregated from training data (K210791 p.8; K233676 p.8). The algorithm-development paper (Tromp J et al., Lancet Digit Health 2022) reports that the workflow was developed on 1145 training echocardiograms and 406 internal-test echocardiograms from the ATTRaCT platform (Asia) with manual tracings by expert sonographers; the strain algorithm (Myhre 2024) was 'trained in an internal dataset' of unstated size. Whether these figures correspond to the training data of the cleared versions (V1.0.0, V2.0.0) is not stated anywhere, so no training-set size is recorded here.

prior_validations.description: Us2.ai press coverage (Sept 14, 2021) of the Us2.v1 clearance cites a validation study at Brigham & Women's Hospital showing automated measurements 'completely interchangeable with expert human measurements' (~2 min processing per study).

Us2.ai regulatory-status page: FDA K210791 (2021) and K233676 (2024); CE Class IIb under EU MDR (certificate 743947); 'approved, registered, or available in 28+ markets'. The page cites regulation 21 CFR 892.1560, which differs from the 21 CFR 892.2050 stated in both FDA letters.

Company platform page: cloud or on-premise deployment, DICOM routing, DICOM-SR/HL7/PDF output to PACS/CVIS/EMR, compatible with GE, Philips, Siemens and handheld POCUS devices; claims a 70% reduction in combined measurement and report-creation time. The 70% figure matches Hirata Y et al., J Echocardiogr 2024 (doi 10.1007/s12574-023-00636-6; 23 patients, single operator).
Company press release (Apr 2024 per web summary) on Us2.v2 clearance: '45 automated echo parameters, including strain analysis'; June 2025 CE release cites 68 CE-marked parameters.

papers.title: A formal validation of a deep learning-based automated workflow for the interpretation of the echocardiogram
papers.key_result: 602 studies from 600 people (421 HF, 179 controls): IEC point estimates all <0 and upper 95% CI <0.25 for 23 parameters vs triplicate core-lab reads; matches the K210791 validation study design (600 studies, 421 HFrEF/179 normal, IEC margin 0.25, BWH core lab).

papers.title: Automated interpretation of systolic and diastolic function on the echocardiogram: a multicohort study
papers.key_result: Workflow developed on 1145 training echos + 406 internal test (ATTRaCT); external validation in Alberta HEART (n=1029), Taiwan real-world (n=31,241), EchoNet-Dynamic (n=10,030) and prospective n=142; view classification accuracy 0.91-0.99; LVEF MAE 6-10%; AUC 0.90-0.92 for LVEF<40%.

papers.title: External validation of a deep learning algorithm for automated echocardiographic strain measurements
papers.key_result: GLS: RMSE 2.61, R 0.84 (Taiwan, 3741 studies analysed); RMSE 2.78, R 0.76 (PROMIS-HFpEF, 176); regional strain AUC 0.80 for wall-motion abnormalities (HMC-QU-MI, 158). Us2.ai employees co-authors; relevant to the strain features added in K233676.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence fully automated analysis of handheld echocardiography in real-world patients with suspected heart failure
papers.key_result: Multicentre prospective study (n=867); AI analysis of handheld echo had accuracy 0.93 (95% CI 0.90-0.95) for LVEF<=40% vs expert cart-based echo; IEC -0.40 (95% CI -0.60, -0.16). Vendor not named in abstract; full text (PMC12803686) identifies Us2.ai software version 1.4.1.

papers.title: Point-of-care AI-enhanced novice echocardiography for screening heart failure (PANES-HF)
papers.key_result: Novices + Kosmos handheld + Us2.ai automated reporting: AUC 0.880 for LVEF<50%; sensitivity 84.6%, specificity 91.4%.

papers.title: Nurse-led home-based detection of cardiac dysfunction by ultrasound: results of the CUMIN pilot study
papers.key_result: Feasibility pilot in Tunisia: 7 novice nurses (5 met the standard), 94 patients, home AI-POCUS vs clinic TTE; AI-POCUS gave an interpretable LVEF in 80% and LAVI in 68%; sensitivity 92% (95% CI 62-99) for LVEF<50% or LAVI>34 mL/m2 vs 87% for NT-proBNP>125 pg/mL (AUC higher for AI-POCUS, P=0.040).

papers.title: Fully Automated Artificial Intelligence Assessment of Aortic Stenosis by Echocardiography
papers.journal: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography
papers.key_result: Us2.ai neural network with no human input vs blinded readers: AV peak velocity r=0.97, mean gradient r=0.94, AVA r=0.88, LVOT VTI r=0.89, LVOT diameter r=0.76.

papers.title: An Automated Machine Learning-Based Quantitative Multiparametric Approach for Mitral Regurgitation Severity Grading
papers.key_result: Fully automated ML MR grading (16 measured parameters, 9 used): accuracy 0.80 for none-to-severe, 0.97 for significant vs non-significant MR (sens 0.96, spec 0.98); feasibility 99.3%. Us2.ai-affiliated authors; MR grading is not part of the FDA-cleared indications.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Echocardiography in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension
papers.key_result: Us2.ai software v1.4.5 vs core-lab readers (213 healthy, 221 PAH): no significant bias for peak TRV (0.90%), RA area (1.71%), TAPSE (1.28%); RVFAC bias 11.46%; PH detection AUC in referral cohort (n=196) 0.75 (DL) vs 0.79 (clinical lab), P=.068.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-based echocardiographic assessment for monitoring disease progression in transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis
papers.key_result: AI-derived LVOT-VTI decrease >=5% over 12 months independently predicted mortality in 752 ATTR-CM patients (adjusted HR 1.41, 95% CI 1.13-1.76). Uses Us2.ai automated measurements (Us2.ai-affiliated co-authors).

papers.title: Clinical and artificial intelligence assessed echocardiographic predictors of outcomes after acute myocardial infarction
papers.key_result: Echocardiograms of 1001 AMI patients analysed with Us2.ai; combined AI-echo + clinical model AUC 0.85 vs 0.81 for 1-year mortality (p=0.018).

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Automated Echocardiographic Analysis and the Workflow of Sonographers: A Randomized Crossover Trial (AI-Echo RCT)
papers.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
papers.key_result: Single-center randomized crossover (UMIN000053259): AI days reduced exam time (13.0 vs 14.3 min, P<0.001) and increased exams/day (16.7 vs 14.1); AI values within clinical limits for 90% of parameters. papers.title: AI task-shifting for echocardiographic LVEF assessment in Singapore: an economic evaluation
papers.key_result: Cost-minimization decision-tree model (PANES-HF pathway): novice-operated AI-POC pathway cost S$1185 (US$1422) per patient vs S$1403 (US$1684) for sonographer TTE, i.e. S$21,669 saved per 100 patients; 99.9% probability of cost saving in probabilistic sensitivity analysis.

papers.title: Validation of a fully automated workflow for longitudinal strain using artificial intelligence

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted peri-operative echocardiography: a multicentre observational study

papers.title: Association of echocardiographic findings with mortality: human assessment vs. automated deep learning analysis
papers.key_result: 889 consecutive hospitalized patients (731 analysable) read by experts and by Us2.ai: strong correlation for most parameters; AI LVEF higher than human by 5.8% on average (P<0.001); 1-year mortality AUC 0.67 (AI) vs 0.66 (human), rising to 0.73 when AI strain was included (P=0.048).

papers.journal: The International Journal of Cardiovascular Imaging

families.summary: Video-based deep-learning module added to the Us2.v2 platform that analyzes apical four-chamber clips to flag adult patients with IVSd or LVPWd >=12 mm who may need follow-up for cardiac amyloidosis. Cleared June 20, 2025 (K250151) under 21 CFR 870.2200 special controls with Ultromics EchoGo Amyloidosis 1.0 (K240860) as predicate; trained on 4,371 patients and externally validated on 1,647 patients from six US and Japanese sites (sensitivity 86.9%, specificity 87.4% among the 87.1% with a confident prediction).
families.intended_use_quote: The primary intended function of Us2.ca is to automatically identify patients who require additional follow-up for cardiac amyloidosis. In doing so, the primary benefit is to improve clinical echocardiographic workflow, enabling clinicians to generate and edit reports faster, with precision and with full control. The final clinical decision of the results still remains with the clinicians.
families.indications_for_use_quote: Us2.ca processes acquired transthoracic cardiac ultrasound images to support qualified cardiologists, sonographers, or other licensed professional healthcare practitioners in their diagnosis of cardiac amyloidosis. Us2.ca is intended for use only in adult patients with increased left ventricular wall thickness, defined as an interventricular septal thickness (IVSd) or left ventricular posterior wall thickness (LVPWd) ≥ 12mm. Us2.ca is not intended to provide a diagnosis and does not replace current standards of care. The results from Us2.ca are not intended to exclude the need for further follow-up on cardiac amyloidosis.

performance_claims.value: AUC 0.89; accuracy 80%; sensitivity 76%; specificity 91%; indeterminate classification in 9% of cases
performance_claims.comparator: Consensus-criteria adjudicated CA diagnosis; controls = 202 suspected ATTR-CA with negative diagnostic evaluation + 114 biopsy-proven extracardiac AL without cardiac involvement
performance_claims.dataset_description: Slivnick JA et al., Circ Cardiovasc Imaging 2026 (doi 10.1161/CIRCIMAGING.126.019610): Amyloidosis Imaging International Consortium registry, 727 CA and 316 controls; used for training/internal validation of the combined AI echo-clinical model and to benchmark the existing Us2.Ca model.
performance_claims.subgroup_notes: Combined AI echo-clinical model (not a cleared function): AUC 0.94, accuracy 90%, sensitivity 93%, specificity 85%, no indeterminate cases.
performance_claims.quote: The AI-ECM demonstrated superior performance (area under the curve, 0.94; accuracy, 90%; sensitivity, 93%; specificity, 85%) compared with the Us2.Ca (area under the curve, 0.89; accuracy, 80%; sensitivity, 76%; specificity, 91%; P=0.006). While the Us2.Ca model classification was indeterminate in 9% of the cases, the AI-ECM allowed classification of all cases.

training_data.description: Training dataset of 4,371 patients (2,241 CA cases; 2,130 controls); ultrasound data from GE, Philips and Siemens systems. Training demographics: CA cases 83% male, 84.6% White, 44.1% aged 71-80; controls 61.7% male, 74.8% Asian; BMI 26.3 kg/m2 both groups. The FDA summary does not name the training sites; the matching development paper (Ioannou 2026) identifies them as the UK National Amyloidosis Centre and Taiwan MacKay Memorial Hospital (CA 2241; controls 2130).
training_data.source: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf25/K250151.pdf (p.12); Ioannou A et al., Circ Cardiovasc Imaging 2026, doi 10.1161/CIRCIMAGING.125.018991

validation_data.description: Independent pooled external validation dataset of 1,647 patients (664 CA, 983 controls) from six clinical sites across the United States and Japan; retrospective routine clinical DICOM; GE and Philips systems only; patient-level analysis (one sample per patient). Confident predictions in 1,434 (87.1%). 'The training and external validation datasets were sourced from entirely separate data providers, ensuring no overlap.'

prior_validations.description: Company press release (July 7, 2025): cardiac amyloidosis feature of the 'AI Echo Copilot' software FDA cleared and CE marked; cites multicenter validation presented at EuroEcho-Imaging 2024 (Ioannou A et al.) with 'datasets nearly twice the size of existing models'.

ASE 2025 abstract listed on the Us2.ai evidence page (Randazzo MJ, Slivnick JA, ... Fontana M, Lang RM): external validation in 1,142 patients across 10 centers (787 confirmed CA, 229 ATTR-negative, 126 non-cardiac AL); AUC 0.87; sensitivity 74% overall / 82% for wall thickness >12 mm; specificity 93%; accuracy 80% / 83%; feasibility 89%. Conference abstract, not peer-reviewed; no DOI.

AI-SCREEN-CA (late-breaking, AHA Scientific Sessions 2025) per company feature page: 11,000+ consecutive patients; sensitivity 82.8%, specificity 95.2%; CA prevalence 16.7% in screen-positive vs 3.0% in screen-negative. Not peer-reviewed; unverified.

Us2.ai-affiliated co-authors.

open_questions: The FDA summary does not state the reference standard used to adjudicate CA cases and controls in the test set (e.g., biopsy, scintigraphy, cardiac MRI).
The narrative states six clinical sites but the data-source subgroup table lists four centers; the site-to-center mapping is not given.
Wall-thickness threshold discrepancy: Form FDA 3881 says IVSd or LVPWd '> 12mm', the 510(k) summary says '≥ 12mm'.
The FDA test set (1,647; 664 CA/983 controls) is larger than the published external test sets in Ioannou 2026 (1,405; 515 CA/890 controls); the additional sites are unidentified.

The company-cited 2026 Circ Cardiovasc Imaging multimodal paper resolves to Slivnick JA et al. (doi 10.1161/CIRCIMAGING.126.019610); its '93% sensitivity and 90% accuracy' describe the combined AI echo-clinical model, not Us2.Ca alone (AUC 0.89, sensitivity 76%, specificity 91%, accuracy 80%). The AI-SCREEN-CA AHA 2025 results remain unresolved to a PMID/DOI.
The 'Others' race subgroup CI (53.51-113.15) and the Hispanic/Latino subgroup (n=5, no controls) indicate very small strata; exact n per subgroup not reported.
Whether Us2.ca is sold as a separately licensed module or bundled in the Us2.v2 platform is not stated.
